concepts.def: Vibration that carries energy without moving matter.
How high or low a sound is.
Distance from one wave peak to the next.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A wave is a way energy travels through a vibration.

Sound waves, water waves, light waves - they all carry energy without permanently moving the stuff they travel through.

Drop a stone in a pond - ripples spread out, but the water doesn't move with them.

Sound is made by vibrations.

A drum skin wobbles, pushing air particles. They bump into the next, and the next. The vibration spreads as a sound wave.

Without something to wobble (air, water, solids), there's no sound.

Pitch = how high or low. Set by frequency (vibrations per second).

Higher frequency = higher pitch (squeaky).
Lower frequency = lower pitch (boomy).

Loudness = how loud. Set by amplitude (size of vibration).

Bigger amplitude = louder. Smaller = quieter.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the motor effect and electromagnetic induction?
options: They are the same phenomenon described in different words.
Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.
The motor effect produces a force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field; induction produces an emf when flux linkage changes.
The motor effect only works on DC; induction only works on AC.

mcqs.q: If air resistance is ignored, which falls faster: a heavy ball or a light ball dropped from the same height?
options: The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
The motor effect only works on DC; induction only works on AC.
Both fall at the same rate because gravitational acceleration is independent of mass.
Heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects because gravity pulls more on them.

mcqs.q: Why does increasing the intensity of light below the threshold frequency not eject electrons?
options: The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
Each photon's energy is below the work function; many low-energy photons can't combine to eject an electron.
Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.
Enough low-frequency photons should eventually eject an electron if you wait long enough.
